pushback.quote: So these are -- you have a very high reasonable surety that these plants have connectivity commissioned and that we will be able to commission 2.5 GW in the next 2 months, just the level of confidence you have for these 2.5 GW in the next 2 months?

Just first on NTPC. Just wanted to check on the decision to participate in Section 63 tenders, there have been about 11, 12 gigawatt of awards. Is this a conscious decision for NTPC not to participate in Section 63, just trying to understand?

pushback.topic: Renewable capacity addition pace and missed targets
pushback.quote: I think last year we missed the target. This year we have capacity target addition of 7 gigawatt. We have done merely 0.6 gigawatt. We understand that there are challenges, but given everything, what are we doing to improve the pace of RE capacity addition in our balance sheet?

pushback.topic: Thermal capacity backing down and technical minimum challenges
pushback.quote: How is NTPC navigating the challenge of select thermal capacity falling below technical minimum in peak solar generation periods? We have heard about NTPC looking to co-locate 5 gigawatt hour of BESS projects at thermal power plants.

credibility.line: Management delivers solid cash flow and profits but routinely adjusts capacity and capex targets due to delays.

narrative_vs_numbers.point: Profit compounding outpaces revenue with PAT reaching INR 27,546 crores in FY26, supporting the operating leverage narrative.
Management lowered FY27 capacity targets to 8 gigawatts on Q2 FY27 from 9,557 MW previously due to persistent transmission constraints.
Cash conversion remains strong with 5y operating cash flow at 216% of profit, backed by Mar 2026 OCF of INR 50,902 crores.

bull: Annual PAT grew to INR 27,546 crores in FY26 from INR 21,332 crores in FY24.
Strong operating cash flow of INR 50,902 crores recorded for FY26 with a 5y cash conversion of 2.16.
D/E ratio improved to 1.31 as of September 2026 compared to 1.48 in FY24.
bear: Borrowings increased to INR 279,526 crores as of September 2026 alongside heavy planned capex.
Transmission and connectivity constraints force downward revisions to renewable capacity addition targets.
Standalone EBIT margin dropped to 6.8% in March 2026 from 20.7% in December 2025.
watch: NGEL capacity addition progress against the revised 8 gigawatts FY27 target.
Borrowings growth relative to equity as D/E stands at 1.31.
Resolution of transmission constraints by mid-July next year.
